terms.comment: The later grammarians’ word, also nōmen dēminūtīvum (Traupman 246). Quintilian says dēminūtum, and dēminūtiō for a diminutive form (1.6.6, Lewis & Short s.v. dēminūtiō).

evidence: Quint. 1.5.46: prō nōmine integrō positum sit dēminūtum (Lewis & Short s.v. dēminuō)

phrases.latin: dēminūtiō genus modo dētegit, et, nē ab eōdem exemplō recēdam, fūnem masculīnum esse fūniculus ostendit
phrases.english: the diminutive form sometimes reveals the gender: to keep to the same example, fūniculus shows that fūnis is masculine
phrases.source: Quint. 1.6.6 (not checked: Lewis & Short cites the passage but does not quote it)
